misconceptions.description: Recording conclusions about engagement or quality before recording the observable behavior
misconceptions.trigger: candidate writes that a tool engaged students without time-stamped, countable evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Record what you could see and count first. Save the conclusion until the observed evidence supports it.

misconceptions.description: Writing observation notes that overlook who got teacher attention and who did not
misconceptions.trigger: candidate notes overall climate but no pattern of access across students
misconceptions.feedback: Track who used which feature and who received check-ins. Access patterns are the evidence a coaching conversation needs.

misconceptions.description: Keeping AI-added claims (such as motivation) that the raw observation notes never recorded
misconceptions.trigger: candidate accepts an AI summary that asserts more than the notes contain
misconceptions.feedback: An observation summary may only state what you recorded. Delete AI interpretation that has no observed evidence.

misconceptions.description: Offering an overall rating in place of verifiable evidence a second observer could check
misconceptions.trigger: candidate submits a one-line verdict or a feature list instead of observed data
misconceptions.feedback: Keep counts, timing, feature use, and access gaps separate from your interpretation so another observer can judge independently.
